data:
go-approx is the home of approximation in the parity plan: interpolation, splines, polynomials, and later Chebyshev and AAA approximation and scattered data.
Package Status Repository interp released v0.2.2 go-approx/interp poly released v0.1.1 go-approx/poly
data.what-is-verified#What is verified: From STATUS.md: numpy.interp, interp1d, PCHIP, Akima and poly1d are bit-identical to NumPy and SciPy; splines agree within 1e-15 to 1e-10. interp v0.2.0 added Splrep (FITPACK’s legacy splrep); v0.2.1 closes the last two gaps, RegularGridInterpolator linear evaluation (7 to 10x faster than SciPy) and shuffled-query cubic evaluation (3 to 9x faster), measured at that release. The timings of the refbench tables of interp and poly are deferred until a run under the load gate. The speed comparison with the Python reference is in interp’s docs/perf.md.
data.where-to-read-more#Where to read more: Landing: go-approx.github.io Documentation: go-approx.github.io/docs Organisation: github.com/go-approx

data:
go-bignum is the home of arbitrary precision in the parity plan: correctly rounded big.Float functions, number theory, and the Go oracle harness.
Package Status Repository bigfloat released v0.2.0 go-bignum/bigfloat
data.state#State: From STATUS.md: v0.1.0 was released with: correctly rounded roots, exponentials and logarithms, trigonometric, hyperbolic and power functions and constants, and the Go oracle harness; the latest release is v0.2.0. At v0.1.0 every function was at or below mpmath’s time (0.18–0.97x at 53–200 bits, 0.27–0.92x at 1000 bits; docs/perf.md), and the results stay correctly rounded against mpmath on 28 840 cases in six rounding modes.
data.where-to-read-more#Where to read more: Landing: go-bignum.github.io Documentation: go-bignum.github.io/docs Organisation: github.com/go-bignum

go-dsp is the home of signal processing in the parity plan: filter design and filtering, spectral estimation, and later resampling, wavelets and audio I/O.
Package Status Repository signal released v0.2.0 go-dsp/signal Timings against SciPy: 28 cases measured on 2026-10-19 were at or below SciPy’s time; the refbench rerun is deferred until a run under the load gate.

go-sparse is the home of sparse linear algebra in the parity plan: sparse containers, orderings, iterative solvers, a quasi-definite sparse LDL^T factorisation (ldl, a port of QDLDL), and later general direct solvers and sparse eigensolvers.
Package Status Repository sparse released v0.3.2 go-sparse/sparse
data.what-is-verified#What is verified: From STATUS.md: iteration counts equal SciPy’s for CG, GMRES, MINRES and LSQR. Six measured spmv, CG and GMRES cases are at or below SciPy’s time. ldl is 1.06 to 1.21x slower than C QDLDL v0.1.9 on the AMD rows, which is an open defect. The refbench table of the package is not yet timed.
